reason: E1 supports the synthesis and thermal/irradiation stability of the specific HEA, but provides no evidence for its use as a diffusion barrier between W and Cu, nor for enhanced transport or void suppression. E2 only motivates HEAs over binary alloys for plasma-facing applications, not interfacial engineering. The key premises about barrier function, transport enhancement, and void suppression are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Refractory HEAs like (CrFeTiTa)70W30 can be prepared by mechanical alloying and sintering
Such HEAs exhibit microstructural stability under high-temperature annealing and irradiation
An HEA interlayer can act as an effective diffusion barrier between W and Cu
The HEA interlayer will enhance electronic and phonon transport, reducing thermal boundary resistance
The interlayer will suppress phase separation and void formation at the W–Cu interface
